sections.overview: Bathylychnops exilis is a large deep-water barreleye, or spookfish, in the family Opisthoproctidae, recorded in the North Pacific and near the Azores.
sections.identification: It can reach about 58 centimetres standard length and is unusual among vertebrates for having a second, ventrally directed optical globe associated with each eye.
sections.habitat: This oceanic species occupies mesopelagic to bathypelagic waters, with records generally between about 400 and 800 metres in the North Pacific and eastern Atlantic.
sections.diet: Its feeding ecology is poorly known; examined stomachs contained krill-like euphausiids, while other possible organic remains have been difficult to identify.
sections.behavior: The striking paired-eye arrangement includes forward or upward primary eyes and auxiliary globes directed downward, giving the fish an expanded field of view.
sections.reproduction: It is egg-laying, and its eggs and larvae are pelagic; available developmental records describe larval pigmentation and body form but little adult spawning behavior.
sections.ecology: Bathylychnops is related to other opisthoproctid barreleyes, including Dolichopteryx; its unusual optics are interpreted as adaptations to dim open-ocean depths.
sections.conservation: No global IUCN assessment was listed by FishBase, and the species is rarely sampled; population size and trend therefore remain unknown.
